utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: The Status Conference is called to order. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-95-10-A, the Prosecutor versus Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. So may I call for the appearances for the appellant, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: My name is William Clegg, and I represent the appellant, Goran Jelisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: May it please Your Honour. I'm Upawansa Yapa. I appear for the Prosecution. Mr. David Leese is the case manager today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear us? Can you hear the English booth?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes. Now it is okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: First, let me ask Mr. Jelisic. Can you hear me? Can you hear the translation? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I can hear it, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now Mr. Clegg.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we proceed to the Status Conference, could I offer an abject and complete apology for the events of Monday of this week when I was not on the end of the telephone link when the Status Conference was last listed. The Court must have felt that I was at least grossly discourteous to the Court for not being at the appointed place at the right time or worse, that I was treating the Court with gross contempt. Neither was in fact the case, and I was mortified to learn that human error in my office had booked the time of the Status Conference two hours removed from the proper time because the time difference between the Netherlands and the United Kingdom had been adjusted in my office in the wrong direction. That is an error for which I must accept and do accept complete fault, and I apologise to the Court for the inconvenience caused. I apologise to Mr. Yapa and the Prosecution team for the inconvenience that I have caused them. And certainly Mr. Hocking and Ms. Belinda Taylor for the time that they gave to arranging the telephone link, all of which was wasted, I extend my apologies to them. And last and by no means least, I apologise to the defendant himself, who was left unrepresented on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you. I take note of that, and I thank you, Mr. Clegg, for this explanation of what occurred on Monday. We have rescheduled, as you have seen, the Status Conference for today. Now, coming to the Status Conference. I am reminded the oral hearings in this case were on the 22nd, 23rd of February, and the Status Conference has the double purpose to allow the parties to express any concern relating to the appeal, to the detention conditions and so forth, and to update the parties with respect to the status of the appeal. Now, as to the first question, let me -- I would like to ask first Mr. Clegg. Is there any problem concerning the appeal or the detention conditions of your client?

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: There is none, but defendant is obviously anxious to know when it might be that the judgement will be given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will give that information soon. Mr. Yapa, any problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. YAPA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not have any matter to be raised at this stage. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as to the status of the appeal, I note that there are no outstanding motions to be dealt with, and I wish to inform the parties that the judgement on appeal will be rendered shortly. I cannot yet confirm a precise date, but a Scheduling Order to fix the date of the hearing in which the judgement will be rendered will be issued shortly, in the next days, in the next days. So without giving a precise date, I can say that the judgement will be issued, in any case, during the next month, possibly not -- towards the end of the month.

utterances.speaker: MR. CLEGG
utterances.text: Could I just indicate that I have informed the Registry that I'm actually in the Republic of China for ten days in July, and if it were possible to avoid the listing of the judgement during those ten days, I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, I take note of that, Mr. Clegg. We'll try to accommodate things, if possible. Well, are there any other matters that the parties want to raise at this stage? Prosecution? No. Well, if that is so, I adjourn these proceedings. This Status Conference stands adjourned.
